title: Building a Privacy-First AI Dashcam System
excerpt: How a fully local vision + VLM pipeline can explain dashcam incidents without sending a single frame to the cloud.
content:
Most dashcam AI products treat the cloud as the default. Video leaves the device, models run remotely, and privacy becomes a policy document rather than an architecture constraint.

This writeup walks through a different approach: a five-phase offline pipeline that keeps every frame on-device while still producing useful incident explanations.

Why offline matters

Dashcam footage often includes faces, license plates, and location context. Shipping that data to a third-party API creates both regulatory and trust problems. A local stack — YOLO for detection, SORT for tracking, optical flow for motion cues, and a local VLM via Ollama — keeps the analysis private by design.

Pipeline overview

The system extracts motion-scored keyframes, fuses object tracking with optical flow to flag incidents, narrates events with a multimodal model, applies privacy blurring, then exports a readable report. Each stage is measurable, so ablation studies can show what each component actually contributes.

Takeaways

Privacy-first AI is not only a compliance checkbox. It forces clearer interfaces between perception, reasoning, and reporting — and those boundaries make the system easier to evaluate and iterate on.

Full architecture notes and evaluation methodology live in the project repository.

title: A Real-time Multilingual Hate Speech Analysis Framework for Penta Language Corpus
excerpt: IEEE conference paper on hate-speech analysis across five Indian languages with transparent risk scoring. Lead author. Accepted; revisions in progress.
content:
Transformer models dominate hate speech detection benchmarks, but many moderation and research settings need decisions that can be inspected, challenged, and audited.

This framework explores a classical NLP path: language detection, language-specific preprocessing, lexicon matching with severity spans, causality heuristics, demographic bias checks, and a composite risk score exposed through a FastAPI backend and dashboard.

What explainability buys you

When a score is high, you can point to the lexical matches, causal patterns, and bias signals that moved the needle. That does not replace human judgement, but it gives reviewers a structured starting point instead of an opaque probability.

Multilingual reality

Supporting English, Hindi, Marathi, Bhojpuri, and Marwari means the pipeline must respect language-specific tokenization and stemming rather than assuming an English-centric tokenizer will transfer cleanly.

Status

Accepted to IEEE conference; revisions currently in progress. Implementation and paper artifacts are available on GitHub.

title: Notes on Shipping Offline RAG Systems
excerpt: Practical constraints that show up when retrieval-augmented generation must run without reliable internet access.
content:
Online RAG tutorials often assume cheap embedding APIs, large context windows, and always-on connectivity. Offline deployments invert those assumptions.

Model size, embedding storage, chunk strategy, and evaluation all change when the system must answer from a local corpus on modest hardware.

Constraints that matter

  • Embedding indexes must fit local disk and memory budgets.
  • Retrieval quality becomes more important than generation fluency when the LLM is small.
  • Fallback behaviour for empty or low-confidence retrieval should be explicit.

A useful evaluation habit

Before tuning prompts, measure retrieval hit rate on a fixed question set. Many generation failures are actually retrieval failures wearing a fluent answer.

Where this fits

Offline RAG sits in the same design family as privacy-first vision systems: keep sensitive data local, make each stage inspectable, and optimise for reliability over spectacle.
